records.title: What TAP is
records.text: TAP is an inscribed token protocol from the Trac ecosystem. Every action is a small JSON object inscribed on a satoshi and tagged with p equal to tap. There is no contract and no sidechain. TAP is an upstream protocol that Bitcoin Universe indexes, not a Bitcoin Universe invention.

records.title: Authority in one picture
records.text: Most TAP operations are ordinary: anybody holding a balance can transfer it. A smaller set is authority bearing and only counts when the authority named by the deployment has signed for it. Ordinary operations are drawn in indigo and authority bearing operations in gold.

records.title: Protocol facts
records.text: Chain bitcoin, network mainnet, protocol tag tap, carried by Ordinal inscriptions, hybrid ownership model, payment and ordinals address roles, ticker up to 32 UTF-16 code units and 128 UTF-8 bytes, decimal scale 0 to 18, partial source coverage, marketplace feature gated behind tapMarketplaceV1.

records.title: Operations at a glance
records.text: token-deploy creates a ticker, token-mint mints under its terms, token-transfer is step one of a transfer, token-send moves a list of items in one authorised payload, and the dmt family carries Digital Matter Theory assets on the tap tag.

records.title: Support in Bitcoin Universe
records.text: Core supports discovery, listing, repricing, unlisting, buying, offers, settlement and reconciliation. Wallet supports view, send and receive. Inscribe supports deploy, mint and transfer. The sell action is unsupported with the recorded reason that TAP has no executable offer workflow on this marketplace surface.

records.title: Related protocols
records.text: TAP on Doge is the Dogecoin variant of TAP, documented in its own repository, with its own indexing and marketplace behaviour. The central portal is docs.bitcoinuniverse.io. Upstream TAP documentation lives at docs.tap-protocol.com.

records.title: Scope and conformance
records.text: This document specifies the TAP profile that Bitcoin Universe indexes. An implementation conforms when it accepts every payload marked valid and rejects every payload marked invalid. A payload that fails any rule is not an operation: nothing moves and the chain records no error.

records.title: Carrier and transaction anatomy
records.text: A TAP operation is the body of an Ordinal inscription, written by Bitcoin Universe as text plain charset utf-8 in a taproot script path reveal. An inscription is identified by txid i index. A negative inscription number is a cursed inscription and its ticker sits in a separate namespace.

records.title: Payload encoding
records.text: Content must be non empty, carry no byte order mark, decode as strict UTF-8, and be exactly one JSON object with string keys and string values. Permitted keys are p, op, tick, amt and dta. No duplicate keys, no unknown keys, no trailing comma, no data after the closing brace. p must equal tap and op must equal token-transfer exactly. dta is capped at 512 UTF-8 bytes.

records.title: Tickers
records.text: A ticker is compared after NFC normalisation and lower casing. It must be at most 32 UTF-16 code units and 128 UTF-8 bytes, with no Unicode control, format or separator characters. Astral characters such as emoji count as two code units each. Negative inscription numbers get a leading hyphen namespace. The Bitcoin Universe inscribe surface accepts 3 characters or 5 to 32 characters.

records.title: Decimals and amounts
records.text: A declared decimal scale is an integer from 0 to 18, defaulting to 0. An amount is an exact JSON string with no sign, exponent, separator or leading zero. Fractional digits must not exceed the scale. Conversion pads and concatenates strings, never floating point. The atomic value is capped at 78 digits and balances can never be negative.

records.title: Operations and per operation fields
records.text: token-deploy takes tick, max and lim with optional prv and dec. token-mint takes tick and amt with optional prv and dta. token-transfer takes tick and amt with optional dta. token-send takes items, each with tick, amt and address. dmt-deploy takes tick, elem, prv and dt with optional id and prj. An unrecognised op is ignored.

records.title: Authority model
records.text: A ticker has an authority only if its deployment named one in prv, and there is no way to add one later. The authority is identified by an inscription holding the public key against which authorised bodies are checked. An authorised body is produced by the authority and carries a salt so it cannot be replayed. Ordinary transfers never consult the authority and cannot be blocked or reversed by it.

records.title: State model and transitions
records.text: Inscribing a token-transfer moves the amount from available to a transferable balance bound to that inscription. Sending the inscription credits the recipient and consumes it. A transfer for more than the available balance has no effect. Sending a live transfer inscription back to its creator settles it at that address.

records.title: Invalidity conditions
records.text: A payload is not an operation when it carries a byte order mark, is not valid UTF-8, is not a single non empty JSON object, has a non string value, repeats a key, carries an unknown key, misses a required key, carries a control character, has a trailing comma or trailing data, fails the ticker rules, fails the amount grammar, or is authority bearing without a valid authorisation.

records.title: Bitcoin Universe indexing decisions
records.text: Source coverage is partial because the writer provides confirmed indexed state and authenticated block digests but no pending mempool feed. Activity for an unknown ticker is quarantined rather than scaled with a guessed decimal scale. Raw records are capped at 256 KiB. The service pins source identity and stores an identity hash in its database.

records.title: The two step transfer
records.text: A TAP transfer is two actions. Inscribing a transfer moves the amount out of your available balance into an inscription you own. Sending that inscription is the moment the balance arrives and the inscription is used up. Between the two steps the inscription is an ordinary ordinal that a careless wallet can spend.

records.title: Worked example: deploying a ticker
records.text: A deployment fixes the ticker, the supply cap in max and the per mint limit in lim. Nothing about it can be changed afterwards. Naming a privilege authority inscription in prv is the decision that gives the ticker an authority, permanently.

records.title: Worked example: minting
records.text: A mint claims an amount into the address that receives the inscription, within the deployment's per mint limit and remaining supply. A mint above the limit does not clamp, it simply does nothing.

records.title: Worked example: transferring
records.text: Step one inscribes the transfer payload. Every character matters: an extra field, a repeated field or a numeric amount means it is not a transfer at all. Step two sends the inscription to the destination. Sending it back to yourself settles the transfer at your own address and returns the amount to available.

records.title: When a token has an authority
records.text: Your ordinary transfer path is untouched by an authority. Minting may be gated, because when a deployment has an authority the mint body can be produced by that authority. An authorised batch send exists at protocol level. Check whether a ticker's deployment carries prv before holding it, because an authority cannot be removed later.

records.title: Mistakes that cost money
records.text: Spending a transfer inscription as change destroys the parked amount. Trusting an unconfirmed transfer is unsafe because there is no mempool feed. Two tickers that look identical on screen can be different tokens. A consumed transfer inscription cannot be reused.

records.title: What Bitcoin Universe supports
records.text: A matrix of what the Bitcoin Universe product code implements across Core, Wallet and Inscribe. It records implementation, not production enablement. Authority bearing operations are not supported on any surface, and the sell action is not supported on Core.

records.title: Buying and selling
records.text: The marketplace treats a TAP position as one live transfer inscription. Before a listing exists the authority must agree with the indexer, the ordinals view and Bitcoin Core at the same checkpoint, and prove the output holds exactly that inscription with no runes and no special sats. Settlement needs one Bitcoin confirmation and the consumed transfer inscription.

records.title: Terminology
records.text: Available balance, transferable balance, transfer inscription, consumed, privilege authority, authority bearing, atomic amount, cursed inscription, quarantine, checkpoint and DMT defined in one table.

records.title: Indexer semantics
records.text: The service pins protocol, chain, network, writer identity, version and revision, and stores an identity hash so a database built for another source cannot be opened. Reads are bracketed by authenticated block digest checks. Source rows are deduplicated by fingerprint. Addresses are Bitcoin mainnet only and mixed case Bech32 is rejected.

records.title: Confirmation states
records.text: A row with a block height is confirmed. A row without block evidence is pending. Statuses of reverted, invalid, orphaned or reorged map to reverted, and failed, rejected or error map to failed. Pending does not mean seen in the mempool: source coverage is partial and there is no pending mempool feed.

records.title: Reorg behaviour
records.text: Reorg coverage is tail replacement only. A bounded tail of each source list is rechecked and invalidations are emitted only when replacement evidence exists. Marketplace reorg reconciliation is automatic: the authority appends observations and reopens or invalidates affected orders deterministically while preserving lineage. Settlement requires one confirmation.

records.title: How TAP differs from BRC-20
records.text: TAP uses the tap protocol tag and the token- prefixed operation names, allows tickers up to 32 UTF-16 code units instead of four bytes, adds an optional dta field on transfers, adds delegated authority through prv, adds a batch token-send, shares its tag with the dmt family and gives cursed inscriptions their own ticker namespace. The two step transfer is identical in both.

records.title: Fees and size
records.text: Every TAP operation is an inscription, so a transfer costs a commit and reveal plus one ordinary send. A minimal transfer payload is under 60 bytes, dta adds up to 512 and a long ticker up to 128. Witness data is discounted, so fixed transaction overhead dominates and batching mints into one reveal is the usual saving.

records.title: Limitations
records.text: No mempool coverage, bounded reorg detection, no indexing of authority bearing operations by Bitcoin Universe, DMT handled by a separate indexer, no numeric freshness policy in the registry, and the sell action not executable. This site does not restate upstream rules it cannot check.

records.title: Security considerations
records.text: For holders: an unsent transfer inscription is a bearer instrument in an ordinary output, tickers can be visually identical but different, an authority is a permanent trust decision, and pending is not settled. For implementers: parse strictly, never use floating point, never infer a decimal scale, bracket reads with checkpoints, check the whole output and require positive evidence to invalidate.

records.title: Implementation checklist
records.text: Payload layer, ticker and amount layer, state layer and operational layer checklists for anyone implementing TAP, covering strict parsing, normalisation, atomic conversion, available and transferable balances, identity pinning, checkpoint bracketing and honest coverage reporting.

records.title: Accepted vectors
records.text: Whitespace with a mixed case ticker and optional data, a negative inscription number producing a hyphen prefixed ticker, a ticker of sixteen emoji at exactly 32 UTF-16 code units, and optional data at exactly 512 UTF-8 bytes.

records.title: Amount conversions
records.text: 1.25 at scale 4 becomes 12500. 1 at scale 8 becomes 100000000. 0 at scale 8 and at scale 0 both become 0.

records.title: Rejected: payload shape
records.text: Duplicate p, an extra unknown field, a nested object as a value, a numeric amount, a trailing comma and data after the closing brace are all rejections, each with the rule that decides it.

records.title: Rejected: encoding
records.text: A leading byte order mark is a rejection rather than something to strip. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 are rejected without substituting replacement characters.

records.title: Rejected: ticker and amount
records.text: A ticker of twenty emoji is 40 UTF-16 code units and fails the limit of 32. An amount of 01 fails the leading zero rule, 1.001 at scale 2 exceeds the scale, a numeric amount fails the exact string rule, and a 79 digit atomic value exceeds the range. Optional data of 513 bytes exceeds the 512 byte cap.

records.title: Rejected: deployment and holder records
records.text: A declared decimal scale of 19 rejects the deployment. A negative holder balance is refused rather than clamped. A mixed case Bech32 address is rejected outright.

records.title: Rule coverage
records.text: A table mapping vectors to the rules they exercise, and naming the rules that need chain state instead of a payload. No authority vectors are published because Bitcoin Universe's TAP indexer does not index authority bearing operations.

records.title: TAP payload validator
records.text: Paste a TAP inscription payload. The tool identifies the operation, checks the fields it requires, explains the authority requirement when the operation is authority bearing, and names the rule behind any rejection. It runs entirely in your browser.

records.title: What it checks, and what it cannot
records.text: It checks the byte level transfer contract, the protocol tag and operation, the field set per operation, ticker limits and form, the amount grammar and atomic conversion, the dta cap and the authority requirement. It cannot check whether the ticker exists, whether the sender has the balance, whether a signature is valid or whether the inscription has been consumed.

records.title: Privacy
records.text: The whole check runs in the page. There is no network request when you press the button, nothing is written to storage and nothing is logged. The only value this site stores is your light or dark theme preference.

records.title: Document version history
records.text: Version 2.0.0 rebuilt this site from a short introduction into a complete protocol dossier with a normative specification, test vectors, a validator, search and corrected repository links. Version 1.0.0 was the initial public introduction.

records.title: Known gaps
records.text: The authorisation format for token-send and the authority inscription format are not specified here at field level because they do not appear in Bitcoin Universe's code in a verifiable form. There are no authority vectors for the same reason. Support claims cover Bitcoin Universe surfaces only.
